topics.topic: Whether open_store may create an absent database or requires it to already exist
questions: Must open_store support an absent database file by treating os.lstat's not-found result as safe and creating it, or must the database already exist so os.lstat can find it?
Must os.lstat be allowed to report that the database path is absent so open_store can create the database, or must the database already exist before open_store is called?

Must open_store support an absent database file by treating os.lstat's FileNotFoundError as an acceptable non-link result, or is the database now required to exist even though the module is required to create it?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P1 on the same unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Whether open_store may create an absent database file or requires it to already exist
quotes: then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link;

Every file and directory the module creates inside data_directory — the database file and its journal, the content-addressed area, the spool area, each run's spool directory, every temporary and every published file — MUST be created owned by the process's effective user and granting no permission to group or others, so that the privacy check of the next start passes on the kernel's own files (A18 rule 2).
precedent.why: The text anticipates creation of the database file but does not say how the required pre-open os.lstat handles a path that does not yet exist.

topics.topic: Whether opening the database must retain an atomic no-follow guarantee after the os.lstat check
questions: Must the database still be opened with a no-follow guarantee in addition to the preceding os.lstat check, or is the non-atomic lstat check intended to replace that requirement?

quotes: then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link;

Every file and directory under the data directory MUST be opened without following symbolic links; a symbolic link met by any call after start makes that call raise StoreInternalError with nothing written.
judgement.divergence: One implementer performs only os.lstat and then a normal SQLite open, allowing a path substitution between the check and open; another retains an atomic no-follow open and rejects such substitution. The owner notices the security difference because the first implementation can open a symbolic-link target outside the data directory while the second cannot.
judgement.why: The open_store-specific passage prescribes a prior os.lstat check, while the broader no-follow rule is framed for calls after start, leaving the database-opening guarantee unresolved.
